attempts.text:
The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Preoperative PSA was elevated at 7.93. The surgical findings included a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2), pathological T2 stage with no extraprostatic extension, positive surgical margins, and no seminal vesicle invasion. Absence of lymphovascular invasion was noted. A key uncertainty is the nodal status, as no lymph nodes were removed, and missing nodal sampling widens this uncertainty. The difference between biopsy and prostatectomy findings is noted, as the biopsy Gleason pattern and ISUP report are missing.

Countervailing factors include the favorable surgical findings regarding local extension and seminal vesicles. The postoperative PSA trajectory and subsequent follow-up are unknown, which significantly impacts the certainty of the prognosis. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and their subsequent trajectory would be crucial to revise this assessment. The current heuristic sensitivity range for recurrence is between 40.8 and 84.8 months.

The patient underwent a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage of pT2, no extraprostatic extension, positive surgical margins, and no seminal vesicle invasion. Lymphovascular invasion was absent, and no lymph nodes were removed. The preoperative PSA was 7.93. The surgical findings, including positive margins, are factors driving the prognosis. The absence of documented nodal status, as no nodes were removed, widens the uncertainty regarding potential recurrence. Biopsy-to-prostatectomy differences are noted as the Gleason pattern and ISUP report are missing. The preoperative PSA level is a significant factor. Prognosis is guided by a heuristic sensitivity range for recurrence, with an expected follow-up without an event at 62.79 months. Information that would revise this prognosis, particularly postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory, is currently absent.
